         Pursuant to Section 215(d)(1) of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Section 39.5 of the

regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”),2 the North

American Electric Reliability Corporation (“NERC”)3 hereby submits for Commission approval

proposed Reliability Standard TPL-001-6 – Transmission System Planning Performance

Requirements. The proposed Reliability Standard 4 would advance the reliability of the Bulk-

Power System by improving how Planning Coordinators and Transmission Planners account for

Inverter-Based Resources (“IBRs”) and Distributed Energy Resources (“DERs”) in their annual

Planning Assessments.

         The proposed Reliability Standard is an integral part of NERC’s proposed framework to

address IBR reliability issues in a comprehensive and holistic manner. The proposed Reliability

Standard addressed in this filing is responsive to the Commission’s directives in Order No. 901

directing NERC to submit new or revised standards enhancing system planning requirements for

IBRs by November 4, 2026.5 As discussed in detail below, proposed Reliability Standard TPL-

I.      SUMMARY

        The TPL-001 Reliability Standard is one of three Transmission Planning Reliability

Standards that set forth Requirements for Planning Coordinators and Transmission Planners to

develop studies of their portions of the Bulk Electric System. The purpose of the standard is to

“[e]stablish Transmission system planning performance requirements within the planning horizon

to develop a Bulk Electric System (BES) that will operate reliably over a broad spectrum of System

conditions and following a wide range of probable Contingencies.” The TPL-001 Reliability

Standard requires each Planning Coordinator and Transmission Planner to perform an annual

Contingencies described in the standard.

        Since the first Transmission Planning Reliability Standards became mandatory and

enforceable, the Bulk-Power System has undergone a remarkable transformation. The resource

mix, once consisting generally of large, synchronous generators, is increasingly comprised of

relatively smaller IBRs and DERs. Such resources have unique technical and operational

characteristics which must be modeled accurately in system studies. NERC and the Commission,

however, have identified deficiencies in how these resources have been modeled, deficiencies

which have implications for the system studies that rely on these models and the actions that are

taken in response to these studies. Several Bulk-Power System events in recent years have

demonstrated the risks to reliability that may result from unexpected IBR performance. Further,

failing to understand the nature and extent of the IBRs and DERs connected to or affecting the

Bulk-Power System can affect how entities plan for the reliable operation of the Bulk-Power

System.

        In recognition of the risks posed by the rapid growth of IBRs, the Commission issued Order

No. 901 in 2023. Order No. 901 highlighted the need for a comprehensive set of Reliability

Standard requirements addressing all manner of issues related to IBR performance, operations,

and planning, to be filed in three phases due in November 2024, November 2025, and November

2026.

        In 2024, NERC completed the development of new and revised Reliability Standards

addressing IBR performance and disturbance monitoring capabilities. In 2025, NERC completed

the development of three revised Reliability Standards, MOD-032-2, IRO-010-6, and TOP-003-8,

addressing the validation of planning System models developed under the MOD-032 Reliability

Standard.

       Proposed Reliability Standard TPL-001-6 would improve the reliability of the Bulk-Power

System by improving how planning entities account for IBRs and DERs when conducting their

annual transmission system Planning Assessments. Proposed Reliability Standard TPL-001-6

would build upon the improvements NERC made in the NERC Modeling, Data, and Analysis

(MOD) Reliability Standards in 2025 to improve how data and models account for IBRs and

potentially impactful DERs and ensure that these improved models are carried forward into

improved Planning Assessments. The proposed standard also reflects several additional revisions

to account for IBR-specific impacts when conducting Planning Assessments. Proposed Reliability

Standard TPL-001-6 addresses in part the last phase of the Order No. 901 directives relating to the

development of new and revised Reliability Standards to improve how entities plan for the reliable

operation of the Bulk-Power System.

III.    REGULATORY BACKGROUND

        A.       Regulatory Framework

        By enacting the Energy Policy Act of 2005,11 Congress entrusted the Commission with the

duties of approving and enforcing rules to ensure the reliability of the Bulk-Power System, and

with the duty of certifying an Electric Reliability Organization (“ERO”) that would be charged

with developing and enforcing mandatory Reliability Standards, subject to Commission approval.

Section 215(b)(1) of the FPA states that all users, owners, and operators of the Bulk-Power System

in the United States will be subject to Commission-approved Reliability Standards. 12 Section

215(d)(5) of the FPA authorizes the Commission to order the ERO to submit a new or modified

IV.     THE NEED FOR REVISED PLANNING STANDARDS ADDRESSING
        INVERTER-BASED RESOURCES AND DISTRIBUTED ENERGY RESOURCES

        A.       The TPL-001 Reliability Standard

        The Transmission Planning (TPL) Reliability Standards set forth requirements for Planning

Coordinators and Transmission Planners to develop studies of their portions of the Bulk Electric

System. These Reliability Standards help improve the reliability of the Bulk-Power System by

requiring planning entities to study how their systems would perform under certain conditions,

system events, and scenarios, and to take actions when studies indicate a system would not perform

as required. The subject of this filing is the TPL-001 Reliability Standard, which addresses

requirements for annual Planning Assessments. There are currently two other Transmission

Planning (TPL) Reliability Standards approved or in effect to address specific planning scenarios

on a five-year timeline: Reliability Standard TPL-007-4 – Transmission System Planned

Performance for Geomagnetic Disturbance Events, and Reliability Standard TPL-008-1 –

Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements for Extreme Temperature Events.

        The Commission approved the currently effective version of the TPL-001 standard,

Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1 – Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements, in

        Like its predecessor versions, Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1 employs a risk-based

approach to the study of Contingencies and the types of corrective action that are required if the

planning entity’s system cannot meet the performance requirements of the standard. For the

system would not meet the design basis laid out in the Reliability Standard. For the scenarios

considered to be less likely but could result in potentially severe impacts (“extreme events”), the

planning entity must conduct a comprehensive analysis to understand both the potential impacts

on its system and the types of actions that could reduce or mitigate those impacts. Entities,

however, are not required to develop Corrective Action Plans to address any system performance

issues identified through these extreme event studies.22

        B.      NERC Identifies the Need to Revise the Reliability Standards Modeling
               Framework to Address the Growth of BPS-Connected IBRs and Distributed
               Energy Resources (Project 2022-02 Uniform Modeling Framework for IBR)

       In late 2021, NERC received a series of Standard Authorization Requests to revise

transmission system planning requirements to address the growth of IBRs on the Bulk-Power

System, as well as the growth of resources connected to the distribution system potentially

impacting Bulk-Power System reliability. These Standard Authorization Requests proposed

projects to improve how Planning Assessments account for the potential impacts of distribution-

connected generating resources on the planning, operation, and design of the Bulk-Power System

and to revise the TPL-001 Reliability Standard to provide clarity and consistency for how Bulk-

Power System connected IBRs are considered, modeled, and studied in transmission planning

assessments.

       To address these Standard Authorization Requests, NERC initiated Project 2022-02 with

the project name Modifications to TPL-001-5.1 and MOD-032-1. While work was underway, the

Commission issued two orders related to IBRs that were relevant to NERC’s work: the first

directing NERC to expand its registry criteria to include non-Bulk Electric System IBRs, and the

second directing NERC to submit a series of proposed new or revised Reliability Standards to

address IBR-related reliability issues, including how entities account for IBRs in system planning

studies. These orders are summarized in the following sections.

       C.      Order No. 901 Directs NERC to Develop Reliability Standards to Address
               Concerns Related to IBRs at “All Stages of Interconnection, Planning, and
               Operations”

development of Reliability Standards to address reliability issues associated with the growth of

 VI.    JUSTIFICATION FOR APPROVAL

       Proposed Reliability Standard TPL-001-6 would improve the reliability of the Bulk-Power

System by improving how planning entities account for IBRs and DERs when conducting their

annual transmission system Planning Assessments. To date, NERC and the Commission have

identified deficiencies in how system models have accounted for IBRs, resources which now

comprise a significant part of the grid’s resource mix and that have technical and operational

characteristics that differ significantly from traditional synchronous generation. These deficiencies

extend to the transmission system planning studies that rely on those models. Proposed Reliability

Standard TPL-001-6 would build upon the improvements NERC made in the NERC Modeling,

Data, and Analysis (MOD) Reliability Standards in 2025 to improve how data and models account

for IBRs and potentially impactful DERs and ensure that these improved models are carried

forward into improved transmission system Planning Assessments.

       The purpose of proposed Reliability Standard TPL-001-6, which is unchanged, is to:

“Establish Transmission system planning performance requirements within the planning horizon

to develop a Bulk Electric System (BES) that will operate reliably over a broad spectrum of System

conditions and following a wide range of probable Contingencies.” The proposed standard would

continue to apply to the Planning Coordinator and Transmission Planner.

       Like the currently effective Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1, proposed Reliability

Standard TPL-001-6 consists of eight requirements addressing the performance of annual Planning

Assessments, identification and mitigation of system performance issues identified through

planning studies, and the sharing of results with neighboring entities. The proposed standard

includes a table, Table 1, that describes the Steady State and Stability Performance Events P1

Background
On October 19, 2023, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) issued Order No. 901 directing the
development of a new or revised Reliability Standard to address reliability concerns related to IBRs at all stages
of interconnection, planning, and operations. In January 2024, NERC ﬁled the initial Standards Development
Work Plan (“Work Plan”) to address the FERC Order No. 901 directives. The Work Plan discusses how NERC will
develop Reliability Standards within three tranches (Milestones 2, 3, and 4) to meet FERC's ﬁling deadlines.
Milestone 4 covers both operations and Planning Assessments. Milestone 4 standards must be ﬁled by
November 4, 2026. All standards must be implemented by 2030.

NERC Project 2025-04 Planning Studies is part of NERC’s Milestone 4 work scope to address FERC Order No. 901
directives related to transmission system planning studies to address reliability risks to the grid from the
application of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs), including both utility scale and behind-the-meter or distributed
energy resources (DERs). A separate Milestone 4 project, Project 2025-03 Operational Studies, is addressing the
remaining Order No. 901 directives regarding operations studies. Both Milestone 4 projects build upon the work
of prior projects in Milestones 2 and 3 to address disturbance monitoring requirements for IBRs and improved
data sharing and modeling for IBRs and DERs.

On December 9, 2025, the Standards Committee authorized the reassignment of TPL-001-5.1 IRPWG Standard
Authorization Request (SAR) and TPL-001-5.1 SPIDERWG SAR from Project 2022-02 Uniform Modeling
Framework for IBR to Project 2025-04 Planning Studies due to the overlapping subject matter.
